name: Pangwali
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: D.D. Sharma, Tribal Languages of Himachal Pradesh (Pangwali sketch); LSI-Himachal Pradesh (Banerjee & Renuga Devi) READ on archive.org but its Pangwali phonology has NO stress statement (length only)
earlier_scan.note: LSI-HP Pangwali chapter read in full: suprasegmentals = vowel length only, stress never stated

sources.citation: Nayak, Binaya Sundar (comp.); eds. G.S. Chouhan, Raj Kumar, Mahatam, Shakuntla Rana. 2011. Prarambhik Pangwari Vyakaran [Introductory Pangwali Grammar] (Hindi). Parmas/Killar: Pangiteam. 48 pp.
sources.note: Sound-system section is orthographic (17 vowel and 31 consonant signs) plus the syllable formula [(C1)V(:)(C2)(C3)]; no balaghat/svaraghat/stress statement (grep: none).

sources.citation: Sharma, D. D. 1989. Tribal Languages of Himachal Pradesh, Part I (Studies in Tibeto-Himalayan Languages II). Delhi: Mittal.
sources.note: Covers Pattani, Tinani, Gahri only. Preface announces 'Part II. Tibeto-Himalayan Dialects of Spiti, Kinnaur and Pangi', but the LDLP grammar write-up (p. 2) reports Pangwali is not in Part II either. The scan's named source ('Sharma, Tribal Languages of HP, Pangwali sketch') is therefore a dead end.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India vol. IX pt. IV: Specimens of the Pahari languages and Gujuri. Calcutta. 'Pangwali' pp. 847-870; Bhadrawah-group comparison pp. 886ff.
sources.note: 'Pronunciation' p. 848: indefinite vowel scale, epenthesis (kur/kuri), j > dz, r-dropping, l-dropping; no accent or stress remark.
Phonology tables sourced to Nayak/Dhanunjay/Rosy 2010; only prosody-adjacent remark is the fossilised vowel harmony (citing p. 16 of that write-up). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Banerjee, Soumi & V. Renuga Devi. [2023 upload; c. 2011-13]. Pangwali. In: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India, Linguistic Survey of India: Himachal Pradesh, pp. 494-568.
sources.note: Phonology sec. 2 (pp. 497ff); '2.b. Suprasegmental feature: Vowel length: Length is not phonemic here' (p. 506) is the only suprasegmental treated; 2.c syllabic structure. No stress/accent/tone/pitch statement anywhere in the chapter (grep: zero hits beyond generic definitions).

sources.citation: [Nayak, Binaya & Dhanunjay]. 2010. Pangwali Grammar Write-up. LDLP (WIn), Pangi. 51 pp.
sources.note: Morphology/syntax only; phonology deferred to the phonology write-up (p. 8). Silent on stress. Its 'Previous research' section (pp. 2-3) states that D.D. Sharma's Tribal Languages of HP announces Pangwali for vol. II but 'it is not found in the second volume'; bibliography lists 'Bhadarwahi-Pangwali Survey Report, 2006. Bangalore: NLCI' and Gibson 1996.

sources.citation: Binaya [Nayak, Binaya Sundar], Dhanunjay & Rosy. 2010 [PDF dated 2013-03-21]. A write-up on Pangwali Phonology. Language Development And Literacy Project (WIn = Wycliffe India), Pangi. Killari dialect.
sources.note: The only work with an explicit stress chapter (TOC: '9 STRESS' p. 75, '10 Practical alphabet' p. 78), but the only PDF ever posted (pangi. 1-30 and 51-55; pp. 31-50 and 56-80 incl. the stress chapter are absent. Surviving pages mark primary stress on some phonetic forms (p. 11: [ɐˈpʰuː] 'your (sg)', [ˈkɐpˑʰɐl] 'when?', [piˈpʰiː] 'spicy', [ˈpʊpˑʰɪ̊] 'paternal aunt', [bɐˈd̪ɛ̤ː] 'cloud', [ˈsʊd̪ˑi], [ˈmɐːsũ], [ˈgʰɐ̤sˑɐ]) and say half-long consonants [Cˑ] occur 'only following short stressed syllable nuclear vowels, or following long vowels' (p. 11) and 'Lengthened variants typically occur followi…

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1908. The Languages of the Northern Himalayas. London: RAS. 'Pangwali' pp. 105-108 ('compiled from two manuscripts', not first-hand).
sources.note: Paradigms and vocabulary only. Sole accent remark is a one-word gloss in the vocabulary, p. 107: 'ghiu (accent on first), ghi.' No general statement.

sources.citation: Pangi.in. 'Introduction to Pangwali language'; 'Pangwali Linguistic papers'; 'Other Linguistic papers' (LDLP/Pangiteam website).
sources.note: No phonology on the pages themselves; they host the three LDLP/Pangiteam PDFs above and summarise other literature (Singh 1998, Verma 1997, Ethnologue, Chaudhry 1998), none linguistic.

sources.citation: Chamberlain, Brad & Wendy Chamberlain. 2019. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Lahul Valley, Himachal Pradesh. Dallas: SIL International (SIL Electronic Survey Report), 185 pp.
